title: Microsoft SC-400 Information Protection Administrator
summary: Exam SC-400 was Microsoft's associate level certification for information protection and compliance administrators, and this page follows the objectives Microsoft published while the exam was live. Microsoft retired the exam in 2025 and moved that certification path to a newer exam, so treat this material as a study reference for the Microsoft Purview skills that carried over. The exam suited engineers who turn legal and regulatory requirements into technical controls for Microsoft 365 data. It covered classification, sensitivity labels, data loss prevention, retention, records management, eDiscovery, audit and insider risk. The exam used multiple choice and scenario based items. A pass signaled readiness to work as a data security or compliance administrator, a role that still exists under the newer credential. Confirm the current certification path on Microsoft Learn before booking. This page is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with Microsoft.

beginner.definition: SC-400 was a Microsoft exam about protecting company data and proving that rules are followed. The full title was Microsoft Information Protection Administrator, and the exam code was SC-400. It asked how you would label sensitive files. It also asked how you would stop them leaving the company. Finally, it asked how long to keep them. Microsoft has since retired this exam, so the same skills now support the newer exam in that path.
beginner.whyItMatters: Companies must protect personal, financial and legal information, and they must show that they do it. People who can turn those rules into working controls are hard to find. The work needs both technical skill and a feel for policy. This exam proved that you can build those controls in Microsoft Purview, the data protection part of Microsoft 365. Even though Microsoft retired the exam, the skills remain in daily demand and they transfer directly to the newer certification. If you already work with data security, that makes this material worth learning.
howItWorks: Start with data classification, because labels, retention and protection rules all depend on it.
Use a Microsoft 365 trial tenant with sample documents so that you can watch a policy take effect.
Study one policy area at a time, such as sensitivity labels, then data loss prevention, then retention.
Write down the order in which conflicting policies apply, because exam questions often test precedence.
Practice reading a business requirement and naming the control that answers it.
Check the current Microsoft objectives, because this exam has been retired and replaced.
beginner.example: Imagine a hospital that stores patient letters in SharePoint. A nurse tries to email one letter to a private address by mistake. If the file carries a sensitivity label, the system can warn the nurse, block the message or encrypt it automatically. Later a manager searches for every document marked as patient data. The search shows that one folder has no label at all. The manager then adds a retention rule. Those letters are kept for the required number of years and deleted afterwards. Each of those steps matches an SC-400 objective, and each one solves a real problem.
takeaways: SC-400 is retired, so use these domains as a skills reference and check the replacement exam.
Classification comes first, because most protection policies depend on it.
Learn how policy precedence works, since scenarios often involve overlapping rules.

chapters.title: Implement information protection
objectives: Create and manage sensitive information types, including custom types and exact data match classifiers
Design, create and retrain trainable classifiers that recognize content by example
Create sensitivity labels and publish them through label policies
Configure auto labeling so that content is classified without user action
Monitor classification and label use with Content explorer, Activity explorer and audit search
Design email encryption with Microsoft Purview Message Encryption and Advanced Message Encryption
Apply bulk classification to on premises files with the Microsoft Purview Information Protection scanner

chapters.title: Implement data loss prevention
objectives: Design and build data loss prevention policies that match the organization's requirements
Configure permissions for data loss prevention and explain policy and rule precedence
Configure endpoint data loss prevention for devices, including onboarding requirements and advanced rules
Analyze data loss prevention reports and activity to separate real incidents from noise
Remediate alerts in the Microsoft Purview portal and in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps
Configure a Defender for Cloud Apps file policy that uses a data loss prevention policy

chapters.title: Implement data lifecycle and records management
objectives: Plan retention and disposition by using retention labels
Create and manage adaptive scopes for retention policies
Create retention policies for SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange Online, Teams and Microsoft 365 groups
Apply mailbox holds and Exchange Online archiving policies
Interpret policy precedence with Policy lookup and explain which rule wins
Build a file plan and manage records, event based retention and disposition
Recover retained content in Microsoft 365

chapters.title: Monitor and investigate data and activities with Microsoft Purview
objectives: Plan regulatory compliance with Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager and manage assessments
Choose between eDiscovery Standard and eDiscovery Premium for a given requirement
Perform searches with Content search and respond to the results
Choose between Audit Standard and Audit Premium, then configure audit retention policies
Investigate user activity in the unified audit log
Configure alert policies and review compliance reports and dashboards

chapters.title: Manage insider and privacy risk in Microsoft 365
objectives: Create and manage communication compliance policies and investigate their alerts
Plan insider risk management, including roles, connectors and policy templates
Investigate insider risk alerts and manage cases and forensic evidence settings
Plan and configure information barriers for Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive
Configure privacy risk management and subject rights requests in Microsoft Priva
